claims.statement: The Prehistoric Society dates construction of Danebury to around 470 BCE.

value.text: The Prehistoric Society dates construction of Danebury to around 470 BCE.

claims.disputeNote: Date disputed: Ford and Saunders (1999), p. 180, describe the site as lasting from 550 to 100 BCE. Reconcile chronologies before choosing a timeline start.

claims.statement: At Danebury, grain was kept in storage buildings and sealed pits.

value.text: At Danebury, grain was kept in storage buildings and sealed pits.

claims.statement: Danebury’s farming community kept sheep and cattle.

value.text: Danebury’s farming community kept sheep and cattle.

claims.statement: Evidence at Danebury includes cereal processing, weaving, leatherworking and metalworking.

value.text: Evidence at Danebury includes cereal processing, weaving, leatherworking and metalworking.

claims.statement: Danebury obtained materials including metals and salt through exchange with other areas.

value.text: Danebury obtained materials including metals and salt through exchange with other areas.

claims.statement: Four rectangular structures at Danebury have been interpreted as shrines.

value.text: Four rectangular structures at Danebury have been interpreted as shrines.

value.text: Hillforts had varied roles; a purely defensive interpretation is insufficient.

value.text: Two wooden cart wheels from Doogarrymore are dated to the fourth century BCE in the museum guide.

gaps: Most British material concerns one Hampshire site; Scotland, Wales, northern and western Britain still need research.
Irish settlement and livelihoods within 500–251 BCE need direct support; earlier Bronze Age evidence is background only.
Reconcile Danebury construction dates and date its activities by phase.
Broad archaeological date ranges do not prove contemporaneity with Socrates.
batch.next: Add excavation-based accounts for other subregions and narrow the candidate dates before timeline publication.

reviewedRelease.note: The regional collection now includes 22 reviewed statements across British and Irish examples, including later Corlea context. Original candidates remain for traceability. Neither regional work package has a complete overview.
